meta.subtitle: Q2 FY27 ARR $5.84B (+25%), net new ARR $333M; a wide-moat franchise fully valued above the Street's target -- HOLD.

analystCommentary: We rate CrowdStrike HOLD with a $220-$305 target range. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, ended July 31, 2026, revenue, ARR, net new ARR and cash flow were all strong: total revenue rose 26% to $1.47 billion, annual recurring revenue grew 25% year-over-year to $5.84 billion, and the company added $333 million of net new ARR, up 51%. Ending ARR from accounts that have adopted Falcon Flex exceeded $2.29 billion, up 101%. Operating cash flow was $530.3 million and free cash flow $377.4 million, both well above the prior-year quarter. GAAP results were thinner: a $33.2 million loss from operations and diluted EPS of $0.01. The problem is price, not the business. At $261.28 the stock trades at 49.6x sales and 208.0x the vendor's forward earnings, above the Street's consensus target of $235.67 (median $245.00, range $132.00-$300.00). We value the shares on consensus EPS and the Street's targets rather than a GAAP multiple. Our probability-weighted fair value is about $255, 2.3% below the current price, against a bear-case downside of 29.6%. That derives HOLD, nearer the SELL line than the BUY line. The Street is more constructive, at 40 buy, 12 hold and 1 sell.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: CRWD), incorporated in 2011 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, provides cloud-delivered cybersecurity through its AI-native Falcon platform, sold on a SaaS subscription model with a single lightweight sensor. The platform protects endpoints, cloud workloads, identity and data, and spans managed security, threat intelligence, next-generation SIEM, identity protection and AI-workload security. The company sells through a partner-first, land-and-expand model: customers start with any number of cloud modules and add capabilities over time, and Falcon Flex, its enterprise licensing model, lets customers commit to a broader platform investment upfront and draw it down across products. Subscription revenue is recognized ratably over the term of the agreement, which is generally one to three years, so reported revenue lags bookings and the ARR base is the leading indicator. The company reports as a single reportable segment and breaks out no product or geographic revenue split. The company description lists alliances with Cognizant and Snowflake and a partnership with Fortanix around AI security.

thesis.body: CrowdStrike is a high-quality compounder whose price already discounts years of that compounding. The bull case is the operating record: ARR of $5.84 billion growing 25%, faster than a year earlier, net new ARR of $333 million, a 74.7% gross margin in fiscal 2026, and fiscal 2026 free cash flow of $1.2 billion at a 25.8% margin, though that margin has slipped for two years. The counter-weight is price: the shares sit above the Street's consensus target, so the multiple, not the business, carries the risk. A relapse in growth, a renewed drag from the July 19, 2024 Incident, or a broad de-rating of high-multiple software would each compress the multiple faster than fundamentals improve. We see a wide moat fully valued, not a bargain.

catalysts: Raised outlook: management raised its fiscal 2027 net new ARR growth outlook after the second quarter, and delivery against it is the next test.
Falcon Flex: ARR from accounts that have adopted Falcon Flex is growing quickly, a sign those accounts are expanding on the platform.
Module expansion: a growing share of subscription customers run six or more modules.
Cash generation: second-quarter free cash flow reached $377.4 million.
AI security: new AI-security work with AWS and Cerebras Systems extends the platform toward securing enterprise AI.
risks: Valuation: the shares trade above the consensus target, leaving little margin of safety if growth or the multiple slips.
July 19 Incident: management expects factors relating to the 2024 sensor outage to keep weighing on key metrics and results.
GAAP profitability: GAAP results are near breakeven, so the equity rests on ARR and free cash flow.
Growth durability: annual growth slowed through fiscal 2026 before the latest quarter turned up; a relapse would hit the multiple.
Competition: the 10-K describes competition as intense, with a risk of losing market share.

financials.incomeCommentary:
In the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (ended July 31, 2026), total revenue rose 26% to $1.47 billion from $1.17 billion a year earlier, and subscription revenue rose 27% to $1.40 billion from $1.10 billion. GAAP subscription gross margin was 78%, up from 77%, and non-GAAP subscription gross margin was 81%. The GAAP loss from operations narrowed to $33.2 million from $105.5 million, while non-GAAP income from operations rose to $371.6 million from $255.0 million; the non-GAAP measure excludes items including stock-based compensation, acquisition-related expenses and July 19 Incident costs. GAAP net income attributable to CrowdStrike was $5.3 million, or $0.01 per diluted share, against a $70.2 million loss a year earlier; non-GAAP EPS was $0.31, up from $0.23.

Growth is where the record turns. Annual revenue growth slowed every year through fiscal 2026, from 54.4% in fiscal 2023 to 21.7%, as revenue rose from $1.5 billion in fiscal 2022 to $4.8 billion. The latest data turned up: second-quarter revenue growth is above that fiscal 2026 rate, ARR growth was 25% at July 31, 2026 against 20% a year earlier, and consensus has fiscal 2027 revenue up 25%. We weigh the upturn as real but early. It rests on one quarter and the fiscal 2027 outlook, and part of it may reflect comparison with periods the company says the July 19 Incident affected through delayed sales and longer sales cycles.

Fiscal 2026 carried a 74.7% gross margin, a -6.1% GAAP operating margin and a diluted loss of $0.65 per share; fiscal 2024 was the one profitable year at $0.30. That annual per-share series appears to sit on a much smaller share count than the quarterly, consensus and guidance figures (guidance assumes 1,044 million diluted shares for fiscal 2027), and the pack does not explain the difference, so we do not compare the two. We use the company's label, the second quarter of fiscal 2027, for the quarter the vendor calls 'Q3 2026'. Prior-year interim figures were revised for an immaterial error found in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.
financials.balanceCommentary: At fiscal 2026 year-end CrowdStrike held $5.2 billion of cash and short-term investments against $0.7 billion of total debt, a net cash position of $4.5 billion. By July 31, 2026, cash and cash equivalents alone, a narrower measure that excludes short-term investments, stood at $5.01 billion. Total equity was of similar size to net cash at year-end, and the current ratio was 1.77, or 1.57 on a trailing-twelve-month basis. Total debt has held near that level across the five-year record while cash and short-term investments rose from $2.0 billion in fiscal 2022, so leverage is not a concern; the -5.0x interest-coverage figure reflects the loss-making operating line, not a solvency issue, because the company carries far more cash than debt. The equity base has more than quadrupled from $1.0 billion in fiscal 2022 even though GAAP net income was negative in four of the five years, so the increase did not come from retained earnings.
financials.cashflowCommentary: Cash generation is the strongest part of CrowdStrike's financial history, but its margin is slipping. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027 operating cash flow was $530.3 million, up from $332.8 million, and free cash flow was $377.4 million, up from $283.6 million. In fiscal 2026 operating cash flow was $1.6 billion and free cash flow $1.2 billion, a 25.8% free-cash-flow margin, after capital expenditure of $0.4 billion. Free cash flow has risen every year since fiscal 2022, even as GAAP earnings stayed near breakeven: the company generally invoices subscription customers at the beginning of the term and recognizes the revenue ratably, so operating cash flow runs ahead of reported income. Conversion has weakened, though. The free-cash-flow margin held between 30.2% and 30.8% from fiscal 2022 to fiscal 2024, then fell to 27.0% in fiscal 2025 and further in fiscal 2026; over those two years operating cash flow grew more slowly than revenue and capital expenditure rose from $0.2 billion. No source in the pack explains the decline, so we treat it as a trend to watch rather than a settled change.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: At $261.28 CrowdStrike trades at 49.6x sales and 208.0x the vendor's forward (NTM) earnings. That forward multiple sits close to the price over fiscal 2027 consensus EPS of $1.26, which is in line with the company's non-GAAP EPS guidance of $1.25-$1.26, so we read it as a current-year multiple. At 162.7x fiscal 2028 consensus EPS of $1.61, the price already extrapolates the consensus path set out under growth. The trailing P/E of -6,531.9x and EV/EBITDA of 2,510.8x carry no information because GAAP earnings are near zero, and the trailing free-cash-flow yield is 0.6%. At these multiples the market prices years of ARR growth near today's pace plus margin expansion, so even a healthy slowdown can compress the multiple faster than earnings grow. Peer multiples are pending a peer data source and the pack carries no history of the stock's own multiple, so we anchor the scenarios to consensus EPS and to the Street: the consensus target of $235.67 sits 9.8% below the current price, the median is $245.00, and the range runs $132.00-$300.00. That the average analyst target implies downside, even as most analysts rate the stock a buy, captures the tension -- a strong business at a price that already reflects it.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: ARR growth holds near today's pace as accounts on Falcon Flex and multi-module customers keep expanding, the raised fiscal 2027 net new ARR outlook is met, and the market keeps paying close to today's current-year multiple as it rolls onto fiscal 2028: an assumed 205x consensus fiscal 2028 EPS of $1.61, just below today's 208.0x, gives about $330, above the Street's $300.00 high.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Revenue tracks consensus and ARR keeps compounding, but the multiple compresses as investors look past the fiscal 2027 upturn to slower growth later, and the shares settle at the Street's median target of $245.00, a checkable anchor that does not move with today's price. On fiscal 2028 consensus EPS that is a current-year multiple well below today's.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Net new ARR growth slows and the July 19 Incident's contraction effects linger, so earnings stall near the fiscal 2027 consensus EPS of $1.26 instead of reaching fiscal 2028's. We value that stalled EPS at the multiple the Street's consensus target of $235.67 places on fiscal 2028 consensus EPS -- a Street multiple that does not move with today's price and still carries a growth premium -- which gives about $184.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: We weight the Base at 45%, the Bull at 30% and the Bear at 25%. That yields a probability-weighted fair value of about $255, 2.3% below the current price, with a bear-case downside of 29.6% to the Bear price of $184. On the derived rule the signal is HOLD, and we rate it HOLD. It sits nearer the SELL line of -5.0% than the BUY line of +10.0%: moving five points of weight from Bull to Bear would derive SELL, so the split is a judgment, not a finding. The Base anchor decides much of that. The case for the Street's median target is that even the consensus target sits below the price although 40 of 53 analysts rate the stock a buy. The case against it is that the shares trade near the top of a 52-week range of $85.68-$263.19, no source in the pack explains a move of that size, and targets may lag it. The Bear reads the consensus target as pricing fiscal 2028 consensus EPS; the pack does not say what basis analysts use. We take stalled earnings at the Street's multiple, rather than a deeper de-rating on top, as the downside case because ARR growth was accelerating at July 31, 2026 and management raised its outlook after the quarter; the Street's low target marks the deeper tail. We give the Bull its weight because net new ARR growth accelerated in the second quarter, and the Bear its weight because a stall needs no collapse in the business, only a slowdown in net new ARR. Our $220-$305 target range brackets the Base implied price and straddles the current price.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: CrowdStrike reports as a single reportable segment and discloses no product or geographic revenue split, so the consolidated total is the reportable line: fiscal 2026 revenue of $4.8 billion, most of it subscription (in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, subscription revenue was $1.40 billion of $1.47 billion in total). Subscription gross margin runs high -- 78% GAAP and 81% non-GAAP in the second quarter -- reflecting the scale economics of a single cloud platform delivered through one lightweight sensor. Professional services are a small complement that the company views primarily as an opportunity to cross-sell Falcon subscriptions. Because the company sells one platform with many modules rather than distinct product lines, the moat is best read at the platform level: more modules per customer, more data, and a stronger network effect.

moatFactors.name: Platform and single-sensor architecture
moatFactors.body: Falcon is delivered as one cloud-native platform through a single lightweight sensor, so customers add modules without deploying new agents. Module adoption is deepening -- 51% of subscription customers run six or more modules, 35% seven or more, and 26% eight or more as of July 31, 2026 -- which raises switching costs and spreads the platform's fixed cost across more revenue per customer.

moatFactors.name: Network effect from data scale
moatFactors.body: The Security Cloud correlates trillions of cybersecurity events per week; the company says that the more data fed into Falcon, the more intelligent its Security Cloud becomes. In our view that is a self-reinforcing advantage a subscale rival would find hard to replicate, and the growing ARR base widens the data and installed-base lead.

moatFactors.name: Land-and-expand and Falcon Flex
moatFactors.body: The land-and-expand model and Falcon Flex let customers commit to a broader platform investment upfront and draw it down across products over time, and ARR from accounts that have adopted Falcon Flex is growing quickly (see growth), a sign those accounts are expanding on the platform. The same structure carries the counter-case. The company warns that if customers are not able to fully utilize their product subscriptions, including in connection with its flexible subscription offering, it may experience increased contraction as they renew with shorter subscription periods, fewer cloud modules, fewer endpoints or smaller contract values. Commitments drawn down over time prove their value at renewal, not at signing.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs
moatFactors.body: Once a customer standardizes on Falcon across endpoints, cloud and identity, replacing it means re-instrumenting security operations. High dollar-based gross retention persisted even through the July 19 Incident, though the incident showed the retention is not unconditional.

businessMoat.durability: The moat is wide but not unconditional. The platform, the data-scale network effect and multi-module adoption make CrowdStrike costly to displace, and ARR and free cash flow have kept growing. The clearest threat is self-inflicted: the July 19, 2024 Incident, whose effects are set out under risks, showed that one faulty update can set back sales even while gross retention holds. The 10-K also describes competition as intense. The second threat is expectations rather than economics: the multiple discussed under valuation leaves little room for a growth relapse. We rate the moat wide and the business durable, but the equity's risk sits in the valuation rather than the franchise.

points: Annual recurring revenue reached $5.84 billion at July 31, 2026, up 25%, with $333 million of net new ARR added in the quarter, up 51%, and $588.6 million over the six months.
Ending ARR from accounts that have adopted Falcon Flex exceeded $2.29 billion, up 101% year-over-year; the figure is the total ARR of those accounts, not spend under Falcon Flex itself.
Management raised the fiscal 2027 net new ARR growth outlook by 630 basis points to 34% at the midpoint and guides full-year revenue to $5,991.1-$6,011.1 million.
Consensus sees revenue of about $6 billion in fiscal 2027, a faster rise than fiscal 2026's, and $7.4 billion in fiscal 2028, which implies growth a little below fiscal 2027's.

AI security is an emerging vector: the company unveiled Continuous Identity for AI Agents, extended Falcon AI Detection and Response (AIDR) to more AI gateway partners, introduced AI, cloud and Next-Gen SIEM innovations with Amazon Web Services, and announced a collaboration with Cerebras Systems on AI inference for enterprises. Separately, an expanded partnership with Schwarz Digits sets a multi-year roadmap to bring Falcon to European enterprises, alongside the agreed purchase of XM Cyber's technology assets.

management.leadership: George Kurtz, the company's founder, is Chief Executive Officer, and Burt Podbere is Chief Financial Officer, as the August 26, 2026 earnings release names them. On the second-quarter results Kurtz highlighted the Falcon Flex results and net new ARR, and Podbere pointed to second-quarter cash flow from operations and free cash flow and to the raised full-year net new ARR outlook. Execution shows in the ARR, net new ARR and free-cash-flow figures set out above. Founder leadership aligns management with the long-term platform strategy, and the July 19, 2024 Incident is a reminder that execution risk is real.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation is investment-led and internally funded. The company pays no dividend and the pack records no share repurchases across the five years, so free cash flow has built the net cash position over that period. Reinvestment runs through research and development and sales and marketing to sustain the land-and-expand model, and through acquisitions that extend the platform -- most recently the agreed purchase of XM Cyber's technology assets from Schwarz Digits. Capital expenditure has risen, as the cash-flow discussion sets out, but remains small beside operating cash flow. Net cash and free cash flow give management capacity to keep investing, to acquire and eventually to buy back stock without outside capital. The cost those figures do not show is stock-based compensation, which the non-GAAP results exclude and which dilutes holders; we would want buybacks to begin offsetting it as the company matures.
management.governance: Governance rests on the 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, filed May 5, 2026). As of April 3, 2026, 254,580,533 shares of Class A common stock were outstanding and no shares of Class B common stock were outstanding, so no separate share class concentrates votes. The excerpt's ownership table lists George Kurtz with the other named executive officers, directors and director nominees. The captured excerpt covers the beneficial-ownership table rather than the board and compensation discussion, so we do not infer board independence, committee structure or pay; related-party detail beyond ordinary beneficial ownership is not in the excerpt.
management.insiderOwnership: Beneficial ownership is disclosed as of April 3, 2026, against the Class A share count above. That count is on a different basis from the roughly 1.02 billion shares behind the current market value, and the pack does not explain the difference, so we read the proxy's percentages as of their date only. George Kurtz beneficially owned 2,384,082 shares, less than 1%, including shares held through trusts and options exercisable within 60 days. All executive officers and directors as a group (11 persons) owned 4,262,065 shares, or 1.67%. Among outside holders, Vanguard Capital Management was listed with 18,449,066 shares, or 7.27%, based on a Schedule 13G filed April 29, 2026, and BlackRock, Inc. with 16,954,069 shares, or 6.70%, based on a Schedule 13G that reports holdings as of December 31, 2023 and may be out of date. Insider ownership is modest in percentage terms, so alignment rests on the founder's role and equity incentives rather than a controlling stake; for outside holders, no insider block can carry or stop a vote.

idiosyncratic: July 19, 2024 Incident: the faulty Falcon sensor update crashed certain Windows systems and has led to lawsuits, claims and inquiries, longer sales cycles, delayed purchasing decisions and customer-commitment packages that included discounting, additional modules, professional services, flexible payment terms or subscription period extensions. The company says those packages have resulted, and are expected to continue to result, in increased contraction, and that certain competitors aggressively approached its customers and partners after the incident. Because customers typically sign contracts with terms over one year, churn and contraction may surface in future periods.
Valuation and expectations: the multiple discussed under valuation embeds sustained high-growth outcomes, so a slowdown in net new ARR or in net retention would leave little valuation support.

Growth and retention: a relapse in the growth upturn discussed under financials would weigh on the multiple, and dollar-based net retention may fall if customers who cannot fully use their subscriptions, including under the flexible subscription offering, renew smaller, the mechanism set out under the moat.

GAAP profitability: fiscal 2026 net income was -$162.5 million and the GAAP operating margin -6.1%, and the second quarter's GAAP net income of $5.3 million was near breakeven. A shareholder therefore relies on free cash flow, and the dilution discussed under capital allocation is the cost of that reliance.

Single-platform concentration: a defect, outage or security failure in the one Falcon platform -- as the July 19 Incident showed -- can affect the entire customer base at once and damage the brand on which new-customer acquisition depends.
risks.systemic: CrowdStrike's results move with the broader technology and macro cycle. Demand for security software is resilient but not immune to enterprise budget tightening in a downturn, which can lengthen sales cycles and slow net new ARR. The equity is a high-multiple, long-duration asset, so it is unusually sensitive to interest rates and to the market's appetite for growth software: a rise in rates or a rotation away from high-multiple names can compress the sales multiple independent of company performance. The company also flags general market, political, economic and business conditions -- including macroeconomic deterioration, inflation, geopolitical conflict and volatility in the financial sector -- as forces that could affect results. As a widely deployed security vendor, CrowdStrike is itself a standing target of cyberattacks, and a compromise of its own systems would harm the reputation on which its franchise depends. These systemic forces bear most on the multiple, which is where the equity's risk is concentrated.

body: We rate CrowdStrike HOLD with a $220-$305 target range that brackets a Base case at the Street's median target. The second quarter was strong on revenue, ARR, net new ARR and cash flow, growth turned up, and the moat is wide. But with the stock above the $235.67 consensus target, the price already reflects that quality, and our probability-weighted fair value sits 2.3% below the current $261.28.

The risk/reward is unattractive rather than outright negative: the Bear, with earnings stalling at the fiscal 2027 level and valued at the Street's multiple, is a 29.6% drawdown, while the expected value sits a little below today's price. The equity's risk lives in the multiple, not the business.

On these scenarios, a rise of a few percent, past the 52-week high, would derive SELL, and a fall toward the low end of our range would derive BUY. Until then we wait. A quarter in which net new ARR growth slows would move weight toward the Bear; net new ARR running ahead of the raised outlook would move it toward the Bull. We also track dollar-based net retention, whether the free-cash-flow margin stops falling, and whether non-GAAP profitability converts into GAAP earnings.
